boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Cove Mountain record (May 10, 1864) in the Crook-Averell Raid on the Virginia & Tennessee Railroad [May 1864]. Averell's approach and his decision against Saltville are context; Cloyd's Mountain (VA049) is Crook's separate battle of May 9. The expedition's marches, the New River bridge fight of May 10, the railroad destruction, the later skirmishes and expedition-wide loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Brigades' and the live page gives zero totals; NPS says Averell met 'a brigade under William "Grumble" Jones'. Averell says he set out with Duffie's and Schoonmaker's brigades, 2,079 officers and men, plus 400 under Oley who were detached toward Crook on the 6th; Pond repeats the 2,079. Averell says Morgan and W. E. Jones had assembled 4,500 at Saltville and that the force he attacked near Wytheville was 'stated by rebel newspapers' at 5,000, mostly infantry with three guns; Pond speaks of Morgan's Saltville forces with three guns. Averell's General Orders No. 5 calls it a superior force.
claims.rationale: Averell's 2,079 is his starting strength, not the number engaged on May 10, and his enemy figures are hearsay (deserters and newspapers). NPS's single brigade and Averell's 5,000 describe different scopes. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live commanders are Brigadier Generals William W. Averell (US) and William E. Jones (CS). Averell says Schoonmaker's two regiments opened the battle while Duffie's brigade formed the line. He names Morgan and W. E. Jones as the Confederate commanders; Pond names only Morgan's forces, and McCausland says Averell 'had been defeated by Morgan near Wytheville'. NPS names Jones's brigade only.
claims.rationale: Who commanded the Confederate force is not settled in the inspected passages; no Jones or Morgan report was inspected. No listed commander receives automatic credit.

claims.value: The frozen result is 'Inconclusive' and the live 'Indecisive'. Averell says he held the field four hours, the enemy retired after dark, and he marched to Dublin. Pond says Averell resisted until night and then made off eastward, and that he was roughly handled by Morgan's troopers; McCausland says Averell was defeated by Morgan and escaped. NPS says the Confederates delayed Averell and then withdrew, and that he burned the New River bridge the next day.
claims.rationale: Which side left the field, and whether it was a check or a defeat, is disputed. The bridge burning is expedition context.

claims.value: The frozen total is 300; the live page gives zero totals. Averell gives his loss in the battle as about 114 killed and wounded; Pond gives 123 killed and wounded for the battle, and for Averell's whole expedition 17 killed, 72 wounded and 34 missing. No Confederate loss for this action appears in the inspected passages.
claims.rationale: Pond's battle figure equals the sum of his expedition figures (17 + 72 + 34 = 123), which include the missing; the relation is noted, not resolved. The live zeros are not measured absence. Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: The reports Averell inclosed and the brigade reports are not printed in the inspected range; Duffie's General Orders No. 18 (read, not selected) praises units in the Wytheville fight. No W. E. Jones or Morgan report was located in the inspected report list.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office; it quotes Crook's and Sigel's despatches and follows Averell's report, so it is not independent of those families. Averell's May 23 report and General Orders No. 5, and McCausland's May 25 report (the targeted follow-up, the only Confederate statement inspected on this action) printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVII, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
